cases.prompt: Harden our refund agent before the launch review. Leadership wants Model Armor and the new semantic policies turned on; the reviewer wants proof that refunds cannot exceed the policy even if a prompt gets through. Tell us what to build and what to prove.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 refund agent behind Agent Gateway, a refund tool that posts to the payments API, a per-refund limit in the instruction, no aggregate bound, screening available but not yet configured. No network or credentials in the session.
assertions: Treats Model Armor and Semantic Governance Policies as a screening layer with its Preview status and the vendor's own accuracy caveat, and keeps the per-refund and aggregate bounds in code that holds with screening off.

Adds an aggregate bound keyed on the business object in the operation record and shows why eight small refunds against one order must trip it (smurfing), rather than relying on a per-call limit alone.
Signs or otherwise integrity-protects the write so an edited amount fails the ledger audit, beside the idempotency key, and names the test for it.
Offers a deterministic policy service as an A2A peer only when a rule must not depend on a model, and does not present the blueprint's simulated anomaly detection as a product.

cases.prompt: We send traces to a third-party OTLP backend. Are our dashboards still using the right GenAI attribute names? I'd like something that warns us when ADK's telemetry stops matching the standard, and I want our nightly judge scores to show up on the traces, not just in BigQuery.
cases.context: An ADK 2.11 agent exporting OTLP to a third-party backend, dashboards keyed on gen_ai.system, a nightly judge writing scores to BigQuery. No network or credentials in the session.
assertions: Rekeys the dashboards on gen_ai.provider.name, gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.agent.name and keeps the gcp.vertex.agent.* keys as ADK-specific joins, explaining that gen_ai.system was removed from the conventions.

Plans the conventions' reference scenario and Weaver live-check as the drift check, diffing against the upstream expected-violation list for google-adk, and records that the scenario is pinned to 2.11.0 and patches ADK's native tool spans.
Emits judge scores as gen_ai.evaluation.result events parented to the evaluated span with the required and recommended attributes and the judge identity, reported as not run without the SDK.
Labels every convention as Development status and does not promise the backend will keep the attribute names.

cases.prompt: Connect our ADK agent to the vendor's remote MCP server. Their authorization server supports client ID metadata documents and our IdP offers enterprise-managed authorization; security wants no dynamic client registration and no per-user consent screens. Tell us how to register, how to bind the credentials, and what the tool contract must survive.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent with mcp 2.x pinned, a remote streamable-HTTP MCP server that speaks revision 2026-07-28, an enterprise IdP, no network or credentials in the session.
assertions: Registers through a hosted Client ID Metadata Document (HTTPS URL with a path, client_id equal to the URL, client_name and redirect_uris present) rather than dynamic registration, and says why DCR is only a fallback.
Keys the stored credentials by the authorization server's issuer, validates a present iss in the authorization response against it, and places both in the credential index the tool-auth skill keeps.

Uses Enterprise-Managed Authorization (token exchange at the IdP for an identity-assertion grant, presented as a JWT bearer grant to the resource authorization server) for signed-in users, and names the client-credentials profile as a draft for headless runs.

Records the mcp major version and the 2026-07-28 revision in the ticket, treats any server-minted state handle as data bound to the caller, keeps tool names inside the specification's character and length rules, and notes that schema keywords ADK's conversion drops must be checked in the recorded-definition test.

cases.prompt: Our booking agent passes the eval set on Monday and fails on Tuesday with no code change. Give us a reliability number we can gate on and a way to grade bookings that doesn't break every time the model picks a different but correct order of calls.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent with a scripted-model test harness and an in-memory booking backend fixture, an eval set of 40 cases, a nightly CI job, no model access in the session.
assertions: Runs each case several times and reports the unbiased pass^k (C(c,k)/C(n,k)), refuses k above the trial count, keeps infrastructure failures out of the denominator but in the report, and defines success from the whole case, not one metric.

Grades bookings by replaying the case's reference trajectory on a fresh backend copy and comparing end states, so a different correct order passes and an extra mutation fails, instead of loosening to ANY_ORDER.
Scores a run that stopped for any reason other than the agent or user finishing as zero, multiplies component results, and treats an undefined criterion as not evaluated.
Pins the judge and model ids in the gate's manifest and states that a judge change starts a new baseline; model-dependent runs reported as not run.

cases.prompt: We have two LLM judges and a set of 60 human-labelled traces; the judges disagree more than we expected. Tell us how to measure agreement properly, and whether we can run our ADK agent under Inspect to reuse its repeated-trial reducers without rewriting the agent.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent, two judge prompts on gemini models, 60 labelled traces with ordinal 1-5 ratings, a scripted-model harness, no model access in the session.
assertions: Reports Krippendorff's alpha at the ordinal level with the level recorded, explains what 1, 0 and negative values mean, and measures each judge against the human labels as well as against each other.

States that the ADK agent can run under Inspect through agent_bridge with Gemini(model='inspect') and a placeholder API key, that streaming mode cannot be bridged, and that this was proven only without tool round trips under a real model.
Treats a NaN or missing reliability figure as not run rather than passed, and keeps ADK's own evaluators and scripted-model Runner tests as the primary evidence.
Pins judge ids and rubric versions, and reports model-dependent runs as not run.

cases.prompt: The platform team standardised on Promptfoo for agent evals. Wire our ADK agent into it so the nightly job asserts on tool trajectories and native spans, and tell us exactly how the job should read Promptfoo's result.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent, Node and Python on the runner, a model key available only in the nightly job, no model access in the session.
assertions: Wraps the agent as an in-process Python provider that calls runner.run_async, returns session state and artifacts for deterministic assertions, and uses trajectory:tool-used, tool-args-match and tool-sequence plus trace-span-count on the native spans.
Maps exit code 100 to block, 0 to pass and 1 to NOT RUN, names PROMPTFOO_PASS_RATE_THRESHOLD as a placeholder until a baseline campaign sets it, and places the job in the model-dependent tier.
Treats repeat with repeat-min-pass as an observed at-least-m-of-n rule recorded beside the figure, not as an estimator, and keeps results unshared unless a share key is configured on purpose.
Keeps the scripted-model Runner tests and adk eval as the primary evidence and labels the Promptfoo guide as vendor guidance to confirm on the installed version.

cases.prompt: Extend our injection test suite so it covers the attack classes the public benchmarks use, without paying for a live red-team run yet, and tell us what a live run would add.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 workspace assistant with mail, calendar, drive and payment tools, a scripted-model Runner harness, no model access in the session.
assertions: Adds cases in the asset's shape for the ported goal classes (split transfer, bulk post-out, code forwarding with trace deletion, steered booking) with invented fixtures, the attribution in the origin field, and end-state assertions through fakes rather than judges.
Keeps the forbidden effects at the gates (allow-list, confirmation, aggregate bound) and asserts the fakes recorded nothing, not that the model refused.

Describes the live route as an adapter wrapping the Runner as a pipeline element reporting attack success rate, as approved paid work with a cost ceiling and version-conditional because the benchmark's API may change.
Imports no benchmark data and reports the Runner tests as not run without the SDK.

cases.prompt: Expose our ADK triage agent over A2A for a partner team and write the acceptance checks for the card, versioning and authentication before we register it anywhere.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 project with a2a-sdk 1.x pinned, one root agent, to_a2a available, a partner that will call with an OAuth client-credentials token, no cloud credentials and no network in the session.
assertions: Writes the card with securitySchemes and protocolVersion, runs agent_card_check.py on it, and lists caching headers, extended-card authentication and cryptographic signature verification as manual checks the helper does not cover (it checks only a signed card's structure).

Names the scoped TCK command against a local to_a2a instance as a planned verification with the requirement ids it proves and the ones deferred (authentication, scripted core operations), never pointing the TCK at Agent Runtime or a registered endpoint.
States that the TCK sends no authentication header, so AUTH-SERVER-002 is verified by the project's own test, and records the run's exit code and reports as the evidence to attach.
Keeps the pins, adds the origin-pinning rule for any raw SDK client that calls the peer, and leaves registration as separate, approved work.

cases.prompt: We expose our ADK triage agent with to_mcp_server. Follow-up questions worked from our old host, but from the new MCP Python client every call forgets the previous one. Find out why, fix it, and add a CI check that would have caught it.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 project with mcp 2.3.0, to_mcp_server over streamable HTTP on Cloud Run with two instances, a scripted model for tests, Node 22 on CI, no cloud credentials in the session.
assertions: Explains that the new client negotiates 2026-07-28 by default, where every request stands alone, so to_mcp_server starts a new ADK session on each call, and that legacy-era continuity also breaks across instances without session affinity.

Chooses an explicit fix (a caller-bound, unguessable conversation handle passed as a tool argument on a hand-built server, or a documented legacy-mode requirement with affinity) and does not claim a server-side switch can disable an era.
Adds an in-process mcp.Client(server) test with a scripted model running the same two-turn exchange under the default mode and mode="legacy", asserting the promised behaviour for each.
Adds a pinned Inspector CLI tools/list step with --format json under --protocol-era legacy and modern, with isolated storage, branching on exit codes rather than piping straight into jq.

cases.prompt: We connect our ADK agent to a partner MCP server whose chart tools ship MCP Apps UI. Nothing shows in our React app or in adk web. Make the charts render in our app and keep the model from calling the partner's UI-only refresh tool.
cases.context: google-adk 2.12.0 with McpToolset (no tool_filter) against a server whose get_chart tool has _meta.ui.resourceUri and whose refresh_chart has _meta.ui.visibility ["app"]; the server registers UI tools only when the client advertises io.modelcontextprotocol/ui. The React app reads ADK events over SSE. No network; nothing installed.
assertions: Explains that ADK attaches UiWidget(provider="mcp") with resource_uri, tool and tool_args but never fetches or renders the HTML, and that adk web 2.12.0 does not render render_ui_widgets.
Identifies that ADK does not advertise io.modelcontextprotocol/ui, so this server sends text-only tools, and records it as a finding or a server-side decision rather than patching ADK internals.
Adds a tool_filter that drops tools whose visibility lacks "model" and requires the backend to refuse view-initiated calls to tools whose visibility lacks "app".

Hands the renderer to adk-frontend-integration: backend resources/read, AppBridge with a null client and backend-routed handlers, a sandbox on a different origin and CSP from _meta.ui.csp; reports tests not run as not run.

cases.prompt: A partner now signs the A2A agent card our ADK orchestrator calls by URL. Make our side refuse the card unless the signature checks out, and tell me what our card checker should flag.
cases.context: ADK 2.12.0 with a2a-sdk 1.2.3 pinned; RemoteA2aAgent(agent_card='https://partner.example/.well-known/agent-card.json'); the partner shared its JWKS URL and key ids out of band; no cloud credentials and no network in the session.
assertions: States that RemoteA2aAgent does not verify signatures on a card it fetches by URL, resolves the card with get_agent_card(signature_verifier=create_signature_verifier(...)) and passes the AgentCard object, and re-applies the https and same-origin check ADK skips for a passed-in card.

Builds the key provider on the out-of-band key set, not on the card's jku; allows asymmetric algorithms only; raises a PyJWTError subclass for an unknown kid so rotation keeps working; and fails closed when verification fails.

Runs agent_card_check.py with --require-signature and --key-host and reads its findings (alg, kid, typ, jku origin, unprotected header, fields the signature does not cover), saying the helper does not verify the signature itself.
Treats a verified card's text as untrusted data for prompts and leaves bearer-token plumbing to adk-tool-auth-and-secrets.

cases.prompt: Our CopilotKit frontend asks users to approve refunds, but since we upgraded the JavaScript client the next message is refused until the approval is answered some other way. Can you fix approvals? And which version of the approval protocol are we actually on?
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent behind ag-ui-adk with emit_interrupt_outcome left at its default, a CopilotKit app on @ag-ui/client 1.0 that answers approvals with useHumanInTheLoop tool messages, require_confirmation on the refund tool. No network in the session.
assertions: Names the two AG-UI approval contracts, diagnoses the mismatch between a 1.0 client that expects interrupt outcomes answered by resume and a middleware answering with tool messages, and makes the ticket declare one contract.

Either keeps the flag off and the tool-message answer, or turns emit_interrupt_outcome on and moves the client to resume, and writes the test that a tool-message answer under the flag returns INTERRUPT_RESUME_REQUIRED.
Uses ADKAgent.from_app with resumability for the paused position rather than the deprecated fire-and-forget constructor path, and strips client-supplied app: and user: state keys.
Keeps the backend confirmation gate as the control (adk-operational-guardrails) and treats the UI decision as permission, not completion; SDK tests reported as not run.

cases.prompt: Our ADK claims agent is exposed over A2A on Cloud Run behind IAM. We want PyRIT to red-team it through A2A and to test whether a poisoned uploaded document makes it file a payout. Set it up.
cases.context: Python ADK 2.12.0, agent served with to_a2a under /a2a/claims, a2a-sdk 1.2.3. PyRIT 1.1.0 is the latest PyPI release. Tools: read_document, file_payout (require_confirmation), send_email. No model credentials in CI.
assertions: States that A2ATarget is not in PyRIT 1.1.0 and needs a later tagged release in its own environment; does not install from git main.
Configures the target with protocol_version auto and the prefixed agent_card_path, and authenticates with an async ID-token provider rather than a static API key.

Models the poisoned document as an XPIA workflow whose processing callback runs the Runner against fakes and returns the executed calls, scored by a substring scorer for the forbidden payout, keeping the scripted-model forbidden-call test as the offline grader.
Labels the live run as approved and paid, with model, date and attack success rate, and keeps a peer injecting into our own agent (ASI07) as a fake-peer test.

cases.prompt: Add garak to our CI so it attacks our ADK support agent itself, not just Gemini, and fails the build on findings. Someone also suggested deepteam's OWASP Agentic preset so the findings come out with ASI labels.
cases.context: Python ADK 2.12.0 agent with read_ticket, issue_refund (require_confirmation) and send_email tools; scripted-model Runner tests exist. CI has no OpenAI or NIM keys; Gemini is available via Workload Identity only for approved live runs.
assertions: Wraps the Runner in a function returning a list of strings and writing a sidecar of executed tool effects, and invokes garak with --target_type function --target_name module#func and --spec, not the deprecated --model_type/--probes.

States that garak exits 0 even on hits and most errors and that its detectors read text only, and gates on the report.jsonl eval rows (fails or nones above 0), a present completion row, a fresh report prefix and the effects sidecar, collecting report and hitlog files from a set XDG_DATA_HOME.

Treats agent_breaker and deepteam as approved paid live campaigns needing a red-team and judge model, keeps the deterministic forbidden-call Runner tests as the CI gate, and maps OWASP IDs from the toolkit's table rather than garak tags.

For deepteam, sets both telemetry opt-out variables, replaces the gpt-4o-mini defaults with a pinned model, notes the sentry-sdk install gap in 1.0.10, and normalises ASI_0n labels to ASI0n without adopting deepteam's titles.

cases.prompt: Our CI has no GCP credentials. Add an offline check that fails the build if any test run leaks personal data or credentials into model requests, session events, logs or tool calls, and tell us whether it can replace the SDP tests.
cases.context: Python ADK 2.12 agent with scripted-model Runner tests, network egress blocked in CI after dependency install, Python 3.12, SDP and Model Armor used in production.
assertions: Keeps exact synthetic-canary sink assertions as the primary check and adds a pinned presidio-analyzer scan over every captured sink as a second, value-independent oracle.
Constructs the analyzer without a runtime model download (NoOpNlpEngine with pattern recognizers, or a pinned pre-installed spaCy wheel) so it runs with egress blocked.
Adds custom recognizers for the project's credential formats because Presidio ships none.
States that the oracle measures nothing about SDP or Model Armor accuracy, does not replace the SDP orchestration tests, and never enters the production path.
Runs it in the existing test framework and reports versions and results as fresh offline evidence.

cases.prompt: Our documents cannot leave our project, so Model Armor on tool results is out. Add LlamaFirewall to screen what our tools return, add its alignment check too, and prove it works.
cases.context: Python ADK 2.12 agent on Cloud Run with fetch_url, read_contract and send_email tools, a scripted-model Runner harness, no Hugging Face token, no model access and no network in the session.
assertions: Places PromptGuard in after_tool_callback on the projected result, chunks it to the 512-token window rather than relying on the scanner's truncation, and loads the classifier once from pre-provisioned weights.
Calls scan_async or the scanner directly, and maps any non-SUCCESS status or unconfigured role to an unknown verdict that withholds the result.

Refuses to enable AlignmentCheck as shipped because it sends the full trace to Together AI under a static key, contradicting the stated residency requirement, and offers the before_tool_callback capability check instead.
Keeps the allow-list, confirmation and egress controls as the enforcement and runs the poisoned-tool case with screening on and off.
Flags the Prompt Guard 2 weights licence as needing an owner decision and leaves the live detector run pending.

cases.prompt: We copied the CaMeL-style before_tool_callback from the security skill. A reviewer says an injected email can still make our agent delete a file or archive a thread. Is our gate really doing what CaMeL does, and what do we change?
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 mail agent with search_mail, send_email, delete_file and a new archive_thread tool added last sprint; capability_gate from injection-patterns copied verbatim; no plan step; no network in the session.
assertions: Finds that the gate allows every tool outside EGRESS_TOOLS and everything when plan:allowed_tools is absent, and replaces it with an explicit read-only set plus one policy per write or egress tool, refusing unregistered tools such as archive_thread.

States that substring taint matching is an approximation a rewritten value evades and that it cannot see a call whose decision was steered by the email, so delete_file must be stopped by plan membership or structure, not argument taint.

Writes per-tool provenance rules (delete and share targets come from the user) and a readers rule for send_email, citing CaMeL as a pattern with a dated arXiv and repository link and no code dependency.

Adds scripted-model Runner tests where the model calls archive_thread and delete_file with an id taken from the email and the gate refuses both without mutation, and reports them as not run unless executed.

cases.prompt: Platform wants every third-party MCP server scanned with Snyk Agent Scan before we adopt it. Add the scan to our adoption checklist and CI without weakening what we already do.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent adopting a vendor's stdio MCP server, CI with containers, a Snyk token in CI secrets, no network in the session.
assertions: Keeps the allow-list, recorded definitions and hash pin as the control and adds the scan as pinned evidence (uvx with an exact version, --ci, exit code read, fields not parsed).
Runs the scan only in an ephemeral container with --dangerously-run-mcp-servers after reviewing the server command, and never against a configuration holding production credentials.

States what the scan uploads to Snyk (configurations, tool names and descriptions, skill content, secrets redacted) under Snyk's terms, offers inspect as the local no-upload mode, and gets the data-handling decision from the owner.
Records that the scan was documented, not run, in the session and that its output schema is experimental.

cases.prompt: We use someone else's remote MCP server, and CI compares its list of tools against a saved copy. Security wants the findings written up using the OWASP MCP Top 10, and they're asking what happens if the server quietly changes a tool's description after we've deployed. We also run a local PDF MCP server inside the same Cloud Run container.
cases.context: ADK 2.12 agent; McpToolset over Streamable HTTP with a list tool_filter and tool_list_cache_ttl_seconds=None; committed mcp_tool_inventory manifest checked in CI; a second McpToolset uses StdioConnectionParams inside the agent container. No network in the session.
assertions: Explains that the CI diff misses a post-deploy definition change and that ADK re-lists on every get_tools without subscribing to list_changed, and proposes a predicate tool_filter that recomputes each tool's manifest hash and withholds mismatches, with a Runner test where the server double changes a description mid-session.
Says a matching hash proves the declared interface, not the server's behaviour.

Reports findings as MCP03:2025 beside LLM03 and ASI04 (and MCP05 or MCP09 for the bundled stdio server), cites MCP ids by id with a link, notes beta status and MCP06's title drift, and copies no OWASP text.
Treats the stdio server as holding the agent's identity and proposes a separate service with its own identity or a sandbox; reports tests as not run.

cases.prompt: Our security team tracks findings against MITRE ATLAS and the CoSAI Risk Map, not OWASP. Review the agent and report findings in their vocabulary without losing the enforcement points.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent with mail, drive and an unfiltered MCP server, RAG over a shared corpus, no budget on turns. No network in the session.
assertions: Reports each finding with its OWASP id and the ATLAS technique id and CoSAI risk id beside it (for example tool poisoning as AML.T0110 and riskToolSourceProvenance; the unbounded loop as AML.T0034.002, riskRunawayAgentToolLoops and controlAgentExecutionBounds), cited by id with links rather than copied tables.
Keeps the enforcement point and observable check for every finding; identifiers never replace the gate.
Takes ATLAS ids from ATLAS 2026.09 rather than the Risk Map's older mappings and says why.
Routes the runtime bound to the guardrails skill and the corpus poisoning to the memory skill, and reports the Runner tests as not run.

cases.prompt: Our refund workflow pauses for a manager's approval that can take days, and a worker restart last week re-issued a refund. Decide whether ADK resume is enough or we need a durable execution engine, and write the test that proves the choice.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 workflow with a refund tool against a payments API that supports idempotency keys, Postgres available, no Temporal cluster yet, no network in the session.
assertions: States that ADK resume runs tools at least once, needs a caller to re-invoke and is unsupported from the web UI and CLI, so a days-long wait with no caller points at an engine, and compares Temporal and DBOS by what the project has (Postgres favours DBOS; Temporal's MCP toolset fixes mcp 1.x; secrets must stay out of Temporal history).
Keeps the idempotency key and reconciliation inside the durable step because an engine checkpoints results and a crash between the provider's acceptance and the checkpoint re-executes the step.

Writes the kill-after-the-write test in both positions (after the tool returns; after the provider double accepted) and the negative control on plain resume, with the engine's replay test added to the suite and reported as not run without the SDKs.
Pins the engine version, records the decision and its evidence in the design, and treats the approval gate as code.

cases.prompt: Our expense agent sends 60% of claims to the finance review queue and reviewers have started bulk-approving it. Product wants escalations under 10%. Lower the rate.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent with decide and escalate tools; the travel and over-500 rules exist only in the instruction; a production escalation-rate dashboard; no labelled cases; no model access in the session.
assertions: Moves the deterministic must-escalate rules out of the instruction into a require_confirmation callable or before_tool_callback, and proves with a scripted-model Runner test that the model cannot bypass them.
Builds labelled cases with a reviewed expected lane and reports missed-escalation and over-escalation rates separately, refusing to tune against the raw escalation rate alone.
Treats missed escalations as the gate and over-escalation as the usefulness target, and keeps the dashboard rate as a drift signal only.
Reports live-model rates as not run.

cases.prompt: Last week a refund approval request sat unanswered over the weekend and Monday's first message executed it. Also, our output screen runs in parallel and sometimes the tool has already fired. Fix both.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent with require_confirmation on the refund tool, a Model Armor output screen configured to run beside the model call, no network in the session.
assertions: Rejects an approval request that is still unanswered when the next invocation starts, records the rejection, and makes a late answer start a new request rather than authorise the old call; tests it with a scripted model.
Makes the approval rule fail closed on arguments it cannot read (missing, malformed, non-object, NaN) by routing to manual review.
Moves the screen that must prevent an effect to a blocking position before the agent and keeps a rejected output's completed tool events while substituting a static data-free message.
Keeps the gate in code and reports the Runner tests as not run.

cases.prompt: Every so often the model rejects a request because our custom summariser plugin left a function call without its result. And nobody here can tell me when compaction actually runs. Can you fix the plugin and pin that down?
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent with App-level compaction plus a custom trimming plugin, a Postgres session store, no model access in the session.
assertions: Treats a function call and its responses as an atomic group that is kept or dropped together and writes the test that a trimmed history never carries a call without its result or a result without its call.
Names the three compaction points (inside the run, before persisting, as maintenance over stored history) with a budget and a test for each.
Measures with the retained-history accounting rather than guessing, and keeps the static instruction prefix intact.
Reports model-dependent checks as not run.

cases.prompt: A user reported that the assistant keeps repeating an old delivery address after they changed it, and last month a prompt injection planted a fake 'VIP discount' memory. Make the memory feature handle both and prove it.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 agent on Vertex Memory Bank with revisions enabled, a nightly generate pass, a gold set with no update or abstention cases, no cloud access in the session.
assertions: Explains that Memory Bank's consolidation updates a memory the new address contradicts and that the test is a knowledge-update case where the new value wins and the old is not surfaced.
Rolls the poisoned memory back to its previous revision by target_revision_id and labels generated revisions by data source so the injection's revisions can be listed and erased.
Adds knowledge-update and abstention cases to the gold set structured by the five memory abilities, measured before and after.
Keeps memory as an untrusted-input boundary with screening before write-back, and reports the live Memory Bank calls as not run.

cases.prompt: Deploy our ADK assistant's FastAPI backend and React app to Cloud Run behind IAP for the pilot group.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 web app built from the designer's web defaults: one FastAPI app with the Runner in process, /api behind a verified-principal dependency, the SPA served by app.frontend(); no cloud credentials in the session.
assertions: Leads with deploy-adk-on-google-cloud and reads its frontend-hosting reference for topology A rather than restarting backend design.
Keeps one process per container with an explicit request timeout and concurrency, and no Firebase Hosting rewrite on run or stream paths.
Uses IAP's signed assertion with the Cloud Run audience form and treats the audience as a fact the first live run confirms.
Presents the exact project, region and commands for approval and reports the live deployment as not run.

cases.prompt: Show each tool call as a line in the chat while the agent runs, and keep the partial answer if the run fails halfway.
cases.context: An ADK web app with a FastAPI backend and a Vite React SPA themed from docs/design/DESIGN.md; the agent route returns JSON today.
assertions: Leads with adk-frontend-integration and its agent-ui-states reference; adk-fastapi-backend is not the primary.
Maps tool start, result and error to one trace line each with status in words, and keeps the text when a run error follows it, marking the turn failed.
Reads the stream with fetch and a bearer token, never native EventSource, and does not send a user ID from the browser.

cases.prompt: We added a table for saved answers. Set up migrations; the agent's sessions already live in the same Postgres.
cases.context: An ADK 2.12 FastAPI app using DatabaseSessionService on Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL; no Alembic yet; tests run against SQLite locally.
assertions: Excludes ADK's five session tables from Alembic with a separate schema or an include_object filter, and prefixes application tables.
Runs migrations as a job rather than at instance start, and leaves ADK's schema to adk migrate session.
Tests that alembic check is clean on a database that holds ADK's tables and that those tables are unchanged.
Filters saved answers by the verified principal and returns the unknown-ID 404 body for another user's record.

cases.prompt: We need an internal assistant that answers questions from our documents and can file a ticket in our tracker. Two developers, roughly 30 hours. A client's team will take it over afterwards, and we'll share the link with a pilot group. Can you design it?
cases.context: A greenfield request in an empty repository; no cloud access; the user answers questions when asked.
assertions: Asks or records the scope question about a web interface, who can reach its URL and whether other developers continue it.
Reads web-app-defaults.md and security-baseline.md and applies tiers 1 to 3 for a handed-over POC reachable at a URL.
Records each SB rule once in the design, with n/a or deferred reasons, and lists companion skills once in the plan.
Writes goals whose acceptance items cite SB IDs beside contracts, and keeps the compact design near 1,450 words.

cases.prompt: /adk-engineer Carry out docs/tickets/doc-assistant/G03.md.
